key_insight: An inverse physics-informed neural network can infer the scrape-off-layer perpendicular heat conductivity as a function of density and temperature by jointly fitting plasma profiles and transport physics.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-efficient way to estimate edge transport properties in stellarators, helping improve plasma exhaust modeling and confinement optimization.
method: Train three coupled neural networks: density profile, temperature profile, and conductivity model κ⊥(n,T).
Constrain the inference with both radial measurements and the residual of a reduced 1D SOL transport equation.
Validate first on synthetic data, then apply the framework to TJ-II helium-beam experimental profiles.
evidence_signal: On synthetic tests, the model recovered the imposed conductivity law with errors below 10% in the data-constrained region and used bootstrap resampling to assess reliability.
watch_item: The inferred conductivity is only as reliable as the reduced transport model and the coverage of the measurement region, so extrapolation outside the trained data range should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks to Infer the Perpendicular Energy Conductivity in the Scrape-Off Layer of Stellarator Devices
